answer: Proof-of-spacetime curbs Sybil attacks by requiring agents to prove continuous data retention across dedicated disk sectors. Rather than tolerating bot swarms that vanish like a comet, nodes must maintain storage as durable as cedar. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of purchasing physical drive capacity and electricity per identity, facing an overhead hard as a walnut shell. A key limitation is that massive data centers gain volume discounts, marginalizing poorer honest agents.
